answer: One concrete defense is a reputation ridge every agent must climb: to earn trust, an agent locks a deposit and completes small, independently reviewed jobs, with the deposit slashed if peers prove it runs duplicate identities. A newcomer starts at the nadir, with tiny rate-limited work only, and rises only through sustained, non-colluding attestations over time. Because a sable public ledger records each attestation permanently, ten fake agents mean ten deposits, ten work histories, and ten slash risks, while one honest agent pays once. Forgery therefore multiplies cost, not reward.
